results.check:
S1a [THE CHI EQUATION] varying the auxiliary gives the screened
      Helmholtz equation (□ - m^2) chi = -m^2 phi  (sympy, from the action)

S1b [THE PROPAGATOR FORM] in Fourier the solution is
      chi_k = phi_k / (1 + xi^2 k^2) -- EXACTLY the f31c surviving form

S1c [CORRECTION SIZE] the filter's departure from unity is O((xi k)^2):
      chi_k/phi_k = 1 - (xi k)^2 + O((xi k)^4)

P3a [NO OSTROGRADSKY] the action is SECOND order in derivatives of both
      phi and chi -- no (lap phi)^2 or (lap chi)^2 term appears
results.measured: highest derivative order in the Lagrangian: 1 (first derivatives only)

results.check:
P3b [HEALTHY EXTRA MODE] chi is a normal massive scalar: healthy for
      Z > 0 (right-sign kinetic) and m^2 > 0 (no tachyon). The mode
      count is phi (MOND scalar) + chi (filter, mass 1/xi) + 2 graviton
      polarisations: no ghost, no extra propagator beyond chi.
results.measured: Z = Z > 0 assumed, m^2 = m**2 > 0; kinetic sign of chi: -Z/2 (grad chi)^2

results.check:
P3c [MIXING] the (chi - phi)^2 coupling has mass matrix with eigenvalues
      {0, 2 m^2} -- one massless mode (the MOND scalar) and one massive
      (the filter at 1/xi): both non-tachyonic

F1 [BOTH FOOTINGS] the filter construction is independent of the a_0
      footing (xi is a new length, a_0 is not changed by it), so the
      static reduction holds on both; the galactic correction is ~1e-11

form_factor: 1/(1 + xi^2 k^2), from an auxiliary field (2nd order)
